Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Crown Minerals Amendment Act 2025 (assent 05/08/2025) s4 replaced 'manage' with 'promote' in the Crown Minerals Act 1991 purpose (s1A(1)); that section came into force 06/08/2025. Commitment met.

Commitment: Explore the potential for a critical minerals list, where such minerals would have a preferential pathway for development once identified.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Government finalised New Zealand's first Critical Minerals List (37 minerals, up from 35 in the September 2024 draft) alongside the Minerals Strategy, launched 31/01/2025. The 'explore' commitment is met by the published list; any preferential pathway operates through general settings (fast-track, RIF) rather than a list-specific regime.

Commitment: Repeal the ban on offshore oil and gas exploration
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Crown Minerals Amendment Act 2025 repealed the petroleum exploration restrictions outside onshore Taranaki (ss 23A(2), 24(5A), 25(2A) and the 'onshore Taranaki region' definition); these provisions came into force 06/08/2025. Commitment met.

Commitment: Increase funding for the Department of Corrections to ensure there is sufficient prison capacity as required.
Invest in the construction of new youth justice beds.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Crown Infrastructure Delivery issued a Registration of Interest for preconstruction services for the Oranga Tamariki New Youth Justice Residences Project (published 10/08/2026, closed 02/09/2026). Budget 2025 gave $33m for improvements at existing residences. New-build residences are not yet under construction.

Commitment: Restore Three Strikes legislation, with amendments to tighten the definition of strike offences and ensure some benefit for pleading guilty.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Reinstated three-strikes regime (Sentencing (Reinstating Three Strikes) Amendment Act 2024) in force 17/06/2025. Covers 42 serious violent and sexual offences, allows limited judicial discretion to avoid manifestly unjust outcomes, and gives a limited benefit for guilty pleas. Commitment met.

Commitment: Abolish the previous Labour Government’s prisoner reduction target.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: PM and Justice Minister announced on 07/02/2024 that the 30% prison population reduction target had been abolished, completing the 100-day plan item. Labour had already dropped the target in September 2023; Corrections told the Minister no action was needed to give effect to the abolition.

Commitment: Take advice on amending the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 so the threshold amount for seizing gang assets is $0 if an illegal firearm is found.
Strengthen the electronic monitoring regime.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Bail (Electronic Monitoring) Amendment Act 2025 (assent 12/03/2025, in force 13/03/2025) lets courts allow EM assessors to approve authorised absences from an EM bail address and validates past Corrections practice. No further legislative or operational strengthening of the EM regime was found in 2025–2026 searches.

Commitment: Rewrite the Arms Act 1983 to provide for greater protection of public safety and simplify regulatory requirements to improve compliance and pass it through all stages during this term of Parliament.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Arms Bill (introduced 08/12/2025, reported back 29/06/2026) received Royal Assent 05/08/2026 as the Arms Act 2026; most of the Act and new Arms Regulations came into force 23/09/2026 (Ministry of Justice). The rewrite repeals and replaces the Arms Act 1983 and passed all stages this term. Cabinet (11/11/2025) dropped semi-automatic law changes, narrowing scope but not the rewrite itself.

Commitment: Transfer responsibility for the Arms Act 1983, policy and regulation to the Ministry of Justice, and transfer the Firearms Safety Authority, administrator of the Act, to another department such as the Department of Internal Affairs.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Delivered with changes. Arms Act policy sits with MoJ. Firearms Safety and Education New Zealand, an independent regulator under the Arms Act 2026, was established 23/09/2026, replacing the Firearms Safety Authority (a Police business unit); MoJ monitors it. Change: the regulator became an independent body rather than moving to DIA or another department, and Police still supply its corporate services.

Commitment: Review whether the Firearms Registry is effectively improving public safety, beginning by June 2024.
Immediately begin to repeal and replace Part 6 of the Arms Act 1983 relating to clubs and ranges.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Arms (Shooting Clubs, Shooting Ranges, and Other Matters) Amendment Act 2025 passed 26/03/2025 (assent 28/03/2025) and came into force 29/06/2025, replacing the 2020 Part 6 clubs-and-ranges controls (MoJ). The 08/03/2024 100-day due date for beginning the work was missed, but the deliverable is in force.

Commitment: Reintroduce partnership schools and introduce a policy to allow state schools to become partnership (or charter) schools.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Education and Training Amendment Act 2024 (assent 30/09/2024) re-established charter schools and a conversion pathway for state schools. The first three charter schools opened 03/02/2025, with four more opening 06–10/02/2025.

Commitment: Explore further options to increase school choice and expand access to integrated and independent schools including reviewing the independent school funding formula to reflect student numbers.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Budget 2025 added $15.661m over 4 years to independent (private) schools, raising the subsidy 11% ($41.6m to $46.2m a year); Education Circular 2025/02 (05/09/2025) sets 2026 per-student rates, paid on rolls from 01/01/2026, so funding tracks student numbers. Charter school pathways (2024 Act) also widen choice. Formula review is in effect done; the open-ended "explore further options" limb has no defined end point.

Commitment: Prioritise reporting and enforcement action to reduce truancy, including centrally collecting and publishing attendance data.
Improve the cost-effectiveness of the school lunch programme.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Remodelled Ka Ora, Ka Ako (announced 08/05/2024) began operating in term 1 2025: by 29/01/2025 Compass-led School Lunch Collective meals at $3 a head were being delivered to intermediate and secondary schools, saving about $130m a year with no change in student numbers. Early delivery and quality complaints followed.

Commitment: Replace the Fees Free programme with a final year fees free policy with no change before 2025.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Final-year Fees Free applies to learners starting their final year on or after 01/01/2025 (IRD), replacing first-year Fees Free. Budget 2026 ends the scheme on 31/12/2026 with no transitional arrangements; claims open until 31/12/2027.

Commitment: Amend the Education and Training Act 2020 such that tertiary education providers receiving taxpayer funding must commit to a free speech policy.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Delivered with changes. Education and Training Amendment Act 2025 in force 19/11/2025. New ss 281A-281B require university councils to adopt a freedom-of-expression statement and complaints procedure, with annual reporting. Change: the duty applies to universities only; Ministers chose not to extend it to polytechnics, PTEs or wānanga.

Commitment: Amend the Education and Training Act 2020 to enshrine educational attainment as the paramount objective for state schools.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Education and Training Amendment Act 2025 (No 65) received Royal assent 18/11/2025 and came into force 19/11/2025. Replaced section 127 makes educational achievement a school board's paramount objective, with attendance and assessment as supporting objectives.

Commitment: Restore balance to the Aotearoa New Zealand’s Histories curriculum.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Final Years 0-10 Social Sciences learning area released 12/08/2026 after about 3,900 submissions; covers NZ history including Māori, settler and migrant experiences alongside world history, civics and financial education. In use from the start of 2027, with two years for schools to fully implement. Seymour said the October 2025 draft delivered ACT's 'restore balance' commitment by dropping the previous 'big ideas'. Held at 75 until the curriculum is in classroom use.

Commitment: Broaden the terms of reference of the Royal Commission into the Covid-19 response, subject to public consultation.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Royal Commission of Inquiry (COVID-19 Lessons) Amendment Order (No 2) 2024 came into force 26/09/2024, establishing phase 2 with new terms of reference covering key 2021-22 decisions (including vaccines and lockdowns) and the economic response, following public consultation on the terms of reference in early 2024. Government decision announced June 2024.

Commitment: Update Pharmac’s decision making model to ensure it appropriately takes patient voice into account and reform the funding model to account for positive fiscal impacts on the Crown of funding more medicines.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Pharmac disestablished its Consumer Advisory Committee on 31/07/2026; an interim consumer committee runs from 01/08/2026 to help set up a new Community and Patient Advisory Committee (recruitment from October, established in the New Year). Francis Review (Apr 2025) found Pharmac's approach not fit for purpose. Patient-voice limb well advanced; funding-model reform to count wider fiscal/societal impacts remains a funded pilot, not a new model.

Commitment: Require the Ministry of Health to publish a Medicines Strategy every three years.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Ministry of Health briefing H2024035858 (21/03/2024) to Associate Minister Seymour proposed developing a new Medicines Strategy, aiming for a draft by end-2024. No published strategy and no three-yearly publication requirement found since; sector groups were still calling for a medicines strategy in late 2025.

Commitment: Better recognise people with overseas medical qualifications and experience for accreditation in NewZealand including consideration of an occupations tribunal.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Health Practitioners Competence Assurance Amendment Bill introduced 18/05/2026; it creates a review committee that can overturn regulators' decisions refusing or limiting registration. Cabinet paper (released Sept 2025) records the coalition's occupations tribunal was considered and a cheaper review committee chosen instead. MCNZ fast-track for UK/Ireland/Australia graduates from 01/11/2024, later expanded via comparable-health-system pathways. Bill not yet passed.

Commitment: Investigate build and lease-back arrangements for new hospitals.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: New Public-Private Partnerships framework released Nov 2024 with Labour backing; it notes long-term leases of private buildings as an alternative for some facilities. Health NZ advised ministers in 2024 that new financing and commercial arrangements may be needed (reported 1News, 01/10/2024). No published investigation of build-and-lease-back for hospitals, and no hospital procured that way, found.

Commitment: Allow the sale of cold medication containing pseudoephedrine.
Allow appropriately qualified pharmacists to directly prescribe certain treatments.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: From 02/06/2026 participating community pharmacies can supply specified funded treatments (child pain/fever, scabies, headlice, conjunctivitis, UTI for women 16-65, ECP) without a prescription under Extended Pharmacy Services. Medicines Amendment Act 2025 (in force 19/11/2025) removed the bar on prescribers holding pharmacy interests and let pharmacist prescribers prescribe unapproved medicines. Not a general power for community pharmacists to prescribe, so held at 50.

Commitment: Agree the terms of reference for the statutory requirement to review the End of Life Choice Act 2019 following consultation between the Parties, with any potential future changes to be progressed by way of a member’s bill, recognising this is a conscience issue.
Notes: MoH statutory review of End of Life Choice Act underway (Act required review by 2024); review report and any member's bill changes still pending. ToR published August 2024; Ministry review and submissions summary provided to the Minister on 7 November 2024 and tabled 20 November 2024. MoH states government parties have agreed any changes will be via members' bills. A draft End of Life Choice Amendment Bill was circulated for consultation in September 2025.

Commitment: Examine the Māori and Pacific Admission Scheme (MAPAS) and Otago equivalent to determine ifthey are delivering desired outcomes.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: RNZ (04/09/2026) and PMN report the Ministry of Health has completed its examination of MAPAS (Auckland) and Te Kauae Parāoa (Otago); it sits with Associate Health Minister Matt Doocey and has not been released. Seymour, briefed on it, says it finds the schemes should continue but disputes its approach. Universities and RACP are calling for release. A Dec 2025 OIA showed the ToR and examination were then under ministerial consideration.

Commitment: Introduce serious penalties for selling vapes to under 18s, and consider requiring a liquor licence to sell vapes.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Delivered with changes. Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Amendment Act (No 2) 2024 raised maximum fines for selling vapes to under-18s from $10,000 to $100,000 (body corporate) and $5,000 to $10,000 (individual), in force 18/12/2024; it also banned disposable vapes. Compromise: no evidence was found that a liquor licence for vape sellers was formally considered; it was not adopted.

Commitment: Implement sanctions, including electronic money management, for beneficiaries who can work but refuse to take agreed steps to find a job.
Notes: Money Management (payment card) and Community Work Experience sanctions live from 26 May 2025; further non-financial sanctions Oct 2025. Electronic money management and sanctions package operational.

Commitment: Develop an approved pool of doctors who can issue medical certificates to go onto a health and disability related benefit.
Remove Section 7AA from the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Oranga Tamariki (Repeal of Section 7AA) Amendment Act 2025 received Royal assent 07/04/2025 and came into force 08/04/2025, repealing section 7AA. Third reading 03/04/2025 (68-54).

Commitment: Create a truly independent monitoring and oversight agency for Oranga Tamariki.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Oversight of Oranga Tamariki System Legislation Amendment Act 2025 (assent 30/06/2025) in force 01/08/2025. It re-establishes the Independent Monitor of the Oranga Tamariki System as a Crown entity with a three-member board, and amends the Children and Young People's Commission Act 2022 (bill aimed to reinstate a single Children's Commissioner).

Commitment: Improve the rights and responsibilities of caregivers to give them more autonomy.
Increase devolution of care decisions to relevant community organisations.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Oranga Tamariki launched Tama-Āriki (05/02/2026), a Māori-designed Enabling Communities prototype run by the Tai Timu Tai Pari collective in Whangārei-Te Kaipara, with $5m to March 2027. It is one of 9 community/iwi prototypes. Minister Chhour has publicly backed devolving resources to communities. No wider devolution policy or legislation found.

Commitment: Immediately issue stop-work notices on several workstreams, including: Three Waters (with assets returned to council ownership), Auckland Light Rail, Let’s Get Wellington Moving, Income Insurance, Industry Transformation Plans, Lake Onslow Pumped Hydro.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: All six workstreams stopped. The Spinoff's 100-day plan tracker (23/02/2024) lists as done stopping work on Income Insurance, Industry Transformation Plans, Lake Onslow, Auckland Light Rail and Let's Get Wellington Moving. The Water Services Acts Repeal Act 2024 came into force 17/02/2024, repealing Three Waters and disestablishing the Northland and Auckland entity, leaving water assets with councils.

Commitment: Amend the Public Service Act 2020 to clarify the role of the public service, drive performance, andensure accountability to deliver on the agenda of the government of the day.
Notes: Budget 2026 announces 8700-job public sector cut and agency mergers (~$2.4b savings), but no specific Public Service Act 2020 amendment identified. Public Service Amendment Act 2026 received Royal Assent and was signed into law; PSC (3 June 2026) confirms it is in force. The Act clarifies the role of the public service, refines chief-executive responsibilities, and strengthens performance and accountability settings.

Commitment: Ensure government contracts are awarded based on value, without racial discrimination.

Issue a Cabinet Office circular to all central government organisations that it is the Government’s expectation that public services should be prioritised on the basis of need, not race, within the first six months of Government.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Cabinet Office circular CO (24) 5 'Needs-based Service Provision' was issued on 13/09/2024 to all ministers and chief executives; it states it gives effect to this coalition commitment. Delivered about three and a half months after the six-month deadline (27/05/2024).

Commitment: Repeal the Canterbury Regional Council (Ngāi Tahu Representation) Act 2022.
Pass the Constitution (Enabling a 4-Year Term) Amendment Bill through first reading in the first 15 months of the term.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Introduced as the Term of Parliament (Enabling 4-year Term) Legislation Amendment Bill on 27/02/2025; first reading and referral to Justice Committee on 05/03/2025, about a week after the 15-month mark (27/02/2025). Reported back 25/08/2025; Government reportedly deferred second reading to next term (Feb 2026).

Commitment: Introduce a Treaty Principles Bill based on existing ACT policy and support it to a Select Committeeas soon as practicable.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Principles of the Treaty of Waitangi Bill introduced 07/11/2024, first reading 14/11/2024, Justice Committee reported back 04/04/2025 (300,000+ submissions) recommending it not proceed; defeated at second reading 10/04/2025 (11–112). Commitment limited to introducing the bill and supporting it to select committee, so the literal commitment is met.

Commitment: Meet with councils and communities to establish regional requirements for recovery from Cyclone Gabrielle and other recent major flooding events.
Make any additional Orders in Council needed to speed up cyclone and flood recovery efforts.
Introduce legislation to remove the Auckland Fuel Tax.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Land Transport Management (Repeal of Regional Fuel Tax) Amendment Bill introduced 20/02/2024, passed all stages 05/03/2024, assent 07/03/2024; the Auckland regional fuel tax ended 01/07/2024.

Commitment: Cancel fuel tax hikes.
Notes: Fuel tax hikes may still take effect after the next election.

Commitment: Introduce legislation to ban gang patches, stop gang members gathering in public, and stop known gang offenders from communicating with one another.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Gangs Legislation Amendment Bill introduced 07/03/2024 (patch ban in public places, dispersal notices, non-consorting orders). Later split and enacted as the Gangs Act 2024 and Sentencing Amendment Act 2024, both in force 21/11/2024.

Commitment: Give police greater powers to search gang members for firearms and make gang membership an aggravating factor at sentencing.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Warrantless search powers for people subject to firearms prohibition orders (including gang members) in force 02/03/2025 via Firearms Prohibition Orders Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (new s18AA Search and Surveillance Act). Gang membership as an aggravating factor in force 21/11/2024 via Sentencing Amendment Act 2024.

Commitment: Stop taxpayer funding for Section 27 cultural reports.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Legal Services Amendment Act 2024 (assent 07/03/2024) in force 21/03/2024; legal aid can no longer pay disbursements for s27 Sentencing Act reports. Pre-approved claims were preserved by a transitional clause.

Commitment: Introduce legislation to extend eligibility to offence-based rehabilitation programmes to remand prisoners.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Delivered through Amendment Paper No 17 to the Corrections Amendment Bill, released 04/03/2024, giving remand convicted prisoners access to offence-based programmes. Enacted in the Corrections Amendment Act 2024 (assent 30/09/2024).

Commitment: Begin work to crack down on serious youth offending.
Enable more virtual participation in court proceedings.
Notes: As at 19/10/2026: Courts (Remote Participation) Amendment Act 2024 (assent 02/09/2024). Audio links in civil and criminal procedural matters in force 03/09/2024; remote observation by victims and support persons (new s9A) in force 02/03/2025.

Commitment: Introduce legislation to repeal the Water Services Entities Act 2022 (Three Waters).
